study: Grade inflation and school competition: an empirical analysis based on the Swedish upper secondary schools (Economics of Education Review 24(3):309-322)
finding: Introduces a measure of grade inflation (grades relative to an external standard) and a measure of school competition; concludes competition does not reliably explain grade inflation, but large gaps appear between public and independent schools and between for-profit and non-profit schools
note: Full text restricted; summary from IDEAS/GUPEA records

study: Betygets värde (Konkurrensverket report)
finding: At that time differences in grading between independent and municipal schools were negligible; independent upper-secondary schools appear to have graded generously around the turn of the century

study: Diskrimineras pojkar i skolan? (IFAU 2010:23)
authors: Tyrefors Hinnerich, B.; Höglin, E.; Johannesson, M.
finding: Blind re-grading of national test essays: the pupils' own teachers gave on average 13% higher grades than external re-graders, i.e. generous internal grading of the national tests

study: Godtyckliga betyg skadar skolan (IFN policy paper)
authors: Hansson, Å.; Henrekson, M.; Vlachos, J.
finding: At three upper-secondary schools more than half of pupils got a higher course grade than their national-test grade; argues grade inflation is more serious in upper secondary school because the course system awards final grades after each course

study: External re-grading of ~32,000 national tests (Skolinspektionen data analysed by Vlachos)
finding: Independent schools gave higher internal grades on national tests than the external re-grading, relative to municipal schools; gap described as modest but consequential

study: The impact of upper-secondary voucher school attendance on student achievement: Swedish evidence using external and internal evaluations (Labour Economics)
finding: Voucher (independent) schools award higher internal grades and grade national tests more generously than municipal schools, while externally graded results are not better (press summary: 'friskolor rättar snällare')
note: Journal details UNVERIFIED (model memory); press coverage sourced. Vlachos 2018 op-ed 'Jo, friskolorna har visst betygsinflation': https://www.ifn.se/media/emhlpoxk/2018-vlachos-jo-friskolorna-har-visst-betygsinflation-förlaga.pdf

study: Statens insatser för likvärdig betygssättning (RiR 2022:22)
finding: Still large differences between grades and national-test results; the 2011 rule that national tests be given special weight had little effect on equivalence; recommends systematic external review where grades and test results diverge

study: Likvärdiga betyg och meritvärden (dir. 2023:95, Henrekson inquiry)
finding: Government inquiry appointed June 2023 'to stop grade inflation'; to propose how grades can be anchored to national tests; report due 21 Feb 2025
note: Outcome (2025 SOU and any bill) not retrieved: see TO-FETCH

study: Betygens utveckling och jämförelser mellan slutbetyg och resultat på nationella prov
finding: Tracks year-9 grades since 1998 (first cohort under goal-related grading) against national-test results

study: Karaktergivning i gymnasiet
finding: Study of how grades affect pupils' approach to learning; notes differing grade distributions across subjects

study: Notat om årskarakterer og prøvekarakterer på stx
finding: Compares teacher-given year grades with exam grades on STX

study: Eksamenskarakterer, almene gymnasier (stx)
finding: Written exam grades on average 0.8 grade points lower than written year grades (årskarakterer)

study: Notat om karakterforskelle i gymnasiet
finding: The tendency to give too-high year grades (relative to exam grades) is becoming more pronounced

study: STUK tilsyn: screening af karakterdata 2023-2024
authors: Styrelsen for Undervisning og Kvalitet / Børne- og Undervisningsministeriet
finding: Screening of 2023 and 2024 data found large discrepancies between year grades and exam grades, especially in mathematics; gap larger for women than men; 2025 results to be added

study: Studenter: karaktergennemsnittet stiger for alle grupper
finding: Averages rose on STX, HTX, HHX and HF 2010-2018; largest rise HTX (+0.9)

study: Comparable Outcomes: Scourge or Scapegoat?
finding: Explains Ofqual's comparable-outcomes method (prior attainment predicts grade distribution) and that it can prevent grade inflation, asking whether that is always desirable

study: Prediction matrices, choice and grade inflation
finding: Describes reference matrices (KS2 -> GCSE, GCSE -> A level) used to predict outcomes; comparable outcomes first officially applied to new GCSEs in 2011 (A levels from 2010 per inter-board comparability reports)

study: Assessing the equivalencies of the UCAS tariff for different qualifications
finding: IB and BTEC found 'overvalued' in the UCAS tariff relative to A levels when judged by later university achievement; recommends redrawing points

study: UCAS Expert Group report on the IB Diploma
finding: Benchmarked three IB subjects against A levels from 2004; a 45-point diploma was allocated 720 UCAS tariff points (about six A grades)
note: Whole-diploma tariff replaced by per-subject points c.2017

study: Grade inflation and the role of standardized testing (in 'Measuring Success', Johns Hopkins UP)
finding: 1998-2016: mean HS GPA of SAT takers 3.27 -> 3.38; A-range share 39% -> 47%; mean SAT 1026 -> 1002; inflation c. 3x faster in private than public schools; top-decile-inflation schools mean GPA 3.56 vs 3.14 in bottom decile
note: Critics note Hurwitz's College Board affiliation

study: Grade Inflation Continues to Grow in the Past Decade (ACT Research)
finding: HS GPA 3.17 (2010) -> 3.36 (2021) among 4.3m ACT-tested students in 4,700 public high schools; held after controlling for student/school characteristics; largest rise 2018-2021; largest in maths

study: High School Grade Inflation and Academically Discrepant College Readiness Indicators (ACT R2514)
finding: Follow-up ACT report; cites the 3.17 -> 3.36 series and examines students whose GPA and ACT score disagree

study: NAEP 2019 High School Transcript Study
finding: Mean GPA of graduates 2.68 (1990), 3.00 (2009), 3.11 (2019) while NAEP 12th-grade scores did not rise

study: NAEP Long-Term Trend, age 13
finding: Progress until 2012; 2012-2020 reading -3, maths -5 points (first decline in LTT history); 2020-2023 reading -4, maths -7 (NCES) or -9 (other reports) points; lowest performers back to 1970s levels in maths
note: Point drops vary between reports; verify against NCES highlights

study: Abiturnoten 2025 (compilation of KMK statistics)
finding: Share of 1,0 Abitur: c.2.2% (2020), 3.4% (2021 peak), 3.1% (2023, 2024, 2025); national mean 2.35 (2025); best averages in 2021 and 2022, slightly worse since
note: dpa reports 2.9% (2020) and >4% each year 2021-2024 on a different base

study: Investigation of final grades vs diploma exam marks (Calgary Herald, reported by Maclean's)
finding: Marks typically fall about 10% when diploma-exam results are added to the teacher mark; much larger drops at some private schools; Alberta Education: 'teacher marks tend to be higher' in every comparison
note: Auditor General (2013) on Nunavut students: classroom grades c. 30 points above Alberta exam results (CBC)

study: Waterloo Engineering adjustment factor (FOI release)
finding: School-specific factor = drop from high-school admission average to first-year average; Ontario mean 16.3%; e.g. Ancaster HS adjusted down 21.4 points for 2022 (Maclean's)

study: Determining ATAR-IB equivalents (ACTAC background paper)
finding: National IB-to-ATAR conversion built as a weighted average of the NSW, Victoria and SA methods; conversion updated for 2022 entry (May 2021) so that not all IB 45s map to 99.95; finer-grained steps from 2023
note: Mechanics of the 2021 change not retrieved; see IBA notices in TO-FETCH

study: SE-CE discrepancy indicator (Inspectie van het Onderwijs)
finding: School-exam (SE) vs central-exam (CE) gap averaged over three years and all subjects; a gap above 0.5 points is judged insufficient and schools must act; gap has narrowed as SE slipped and CE rose
note: VO-raad: inspectorate 'for now' not enforcing the indicator (date unknown)

study: Matriculation exam vs course grades, Southern Finland (JSSE)
finding: 6,172 students: subject-exam grades correlated strongly with course grades across three years; Board sets grade cut-offs after assessment, target c. 5% L and 15% E

study: Leaving Certificate post-pandemic adjustment
authors: State Examinations Commission / Department of Education
finding: H1 share 14.3% (2024) -> 11.7% (2025) -> 10.1% (2026); H4+ share 62.9% (2019) -> 77.2% (2023) -> 74.2% (2024); 'artificial boost' cut from 7.5% to 5.5% in 2025 with multi-year return to 2019 standards
